description: Dynamically adjust the chunk size for speculative parallel parsing based on the local entropy of the JSON input. High-entropy regions (dense strings, varied data) benefit from larger chunks to amortize speculation overhead, while low-entropy regions (repeated structure, arrays of similar objects) can use smaller chunks for finer parallelism. Borrowed from adaptive compression algorithms that adjust window sizes based on source entropy.
mathematical_formalization: Estimate local entropy H(C_i) = -sum_b p(b) log p(b) for each chunk C_i using byte frequency counts. Define optimal chunk size: L_opt(H) = L_min * 2^(alpha * H / H_max) where alpha controls the sensitivity. The speculation miss rate for JSON correlates with string density: P_miss ~ f_string * (1 - e^{-L/lambda}) where lambda is the average string length. Minimizing total cost: argmin_L { n/(L*P) * T_chunk + n/L * P_miss(L) * T_fixup }.
analogical_connections: Adaptive Huffman coding: adjusts code tables based on observed symbol frequencies; here we adjust parallelism granularity
TCP congestion window: dynamically sizes the transmission window based on network conditions; here we size parse chunks based on data conditions
Adaptive mesh refinement in CFD: refine the grid where the solution has high gradients; here refine parallelism where the data has high structural complexity
implementation_hypothesis: First pass: scan input at 4KB granularity to compute byte frequency histograms (using VPOPCNT on byte classifications). Compute entropy estimate per 4KB block. Group blocks into variable-sized chunks where chunk boundaries are placed at low-entropy points (e.g., between array elements). Feed the variable-sized chunks to the speculative parallel indexer. The grouping overhead is O(n/4096) and can itself be SIMD-accelerated.
experiment_seed: Profile speculation miss rates across different JSON files as a function of chunk size. Fit the P_miss(L) model empirically. Implement the entropy-adaptive chunking and compare against fixed-size chunking. Measure: (1) overall speculation miss rate, (2) throughput variation, (3) load balance across cores. Target: reduce speculation misses by >50% compared to fixed-size chunks on heterogeneous JSON inputs.
